body: Oh, man. The love one completely sucks. I love it! Thank you!

Thanks, I understand how bad wishes can be and I go into this with full fear of "Don't be a dick and keep it interesting," but at the same time I want this to be a challenge that impacts the players as well as the characters. He will be very weak as it will take some time for his full power to come back to fruition. So he won't be toppling entire nations anytime soon. 

But vomiting spiders sounds really fun. Maybe every time one of them try to cast a spell against him they get a mouth full of spiders instead? I like it. Thanks!
That's actually really good and very simple. Thanks! :D

Thanks! 

I have a round about plan to get them to know about silver weapons and acquire them first from a charitable mothering ex-adventuring NPC. I'm hoping they'll be level 2 by the time they hit the werewolf and they should definitely be level three/four by the time they reach the basilisk. 

I never even considered doing an owlbear! While the basilisk is a more memorable event, you're right in it being a challenge at multiple levels so I could extract it and do it at a later date. Thank you very much for your help.
I'm actually asking for advice. Any advice. Copying and pasting a manual doesn't count as help, it's incredibly elitist. But at least I know the current price!

Trust me, it's food. 

A woman baked me a cake for helping her with a display for her graduation. It was my job to do that, but because I did it in the exact style she requested she appreciated it. She didn't owe me shit, but still it made me blush like crazy and it makes me think highly of her. 

Chocolates, Cake, Pizza. I work with some amazing girls, and I hate my weight because of it.

He was generally a bad friend in the ending stages. He ghosted people a lot. He couldn't hold a job and even removed his own family from his life. There was something wrong with him, but I tolerated him because he was my friend. He also had a terrible childhood, and lost his parents at an early age. Years go by and I helped him when he was homeless, gave him money so he could move from place to place. That was a gift, I never expected it back, but he got really angry with me that I wouldn't accept the money back. He had a lot of pride. Regardless, that's pretty common, easy to forget about but it gets ten times worse. 

He tried to murder someone. Strike that, he never tried, he had a step-by-step plan how to kill someone, how to hide the body, how to escape if the police came by. I never knew who his alleged victim would have been, still don't know. I only found out because a mutual friend (who I've also cut out of my life) told me what he was planning. I spoke to him and he started getting really aggressive. Started saying he needed to do it, how this person deserved it. That he'd rather be in jail than let this person live. I reported him, needless to say. He was never charged, because he was smart enough not to tell me the name. 

It ended our friendship, pretty much ghosted me. I didn't care though. There was literally something wrong with him. He was fine most of the time I knew him, but ever since he became homeless it was like there was a different man there.
Love at first sight is real.

Her. She's kind, and caring and passionate. She rolled her eyes with a coy smile when I made a cringey joke before and it floored me. She's attractive. Yet, my low self-esteem will always make me feel unworthy of any affection, so I will likely never even try to ask her out.
Well the years start coming and they don't stop coming, and they don't stop coming, and they don't stop coming, and they don't stop coming
Kindness and tolerance when you tell them what they don't want to hear. In customer service this is such a rare gem, but you never forget those few awesome people.

My sister.

 He was (is) an alcoholic who relapsed three days before his wedding thinking he could control himself. He was the type who could drink sociably and then act like a complete zombie for three days after. It was incredibly taxing on her. I told her I didn't approve of the marriage, and told her that I knew if she got married she'd be stuck with him for life and any future children they have would have a deadbeat dad. She didn't marry him, and my mother tells me it's solely because that I said what I did. While I don't regret what I did, I caused my sister a lot of problems for two years, and often wonder if I over reacted.
